subject: Urban Planning
title: Transfer of Development Rights
description: A fast breakdown of Transfer of Development Rights for builders.

hook.text: What if a farmer could sell the right to develop land — without selling the farm itself?

buildup.text: TDR programs let landowners in protected areas sell development rights to builders in growth zones.

discovery.text: The farm stays farmland forever. The builder gets extra density in the city. Both sides benefit financially.

twist.text: TDR is elegant in theory but complex in practice. Markets for development rights are thin and hard to manage.

climax.text: New York and Montgomery County, Maryland have the most successful TDR programs in the country.

punchline.text: Protect the farm. Build in the city. Trade the rights between them.

quiz.question: How do Transfer of Development Rights programs work?
options: The government buys all development rights and redistributes them equally
Landowners in protected areas sell development rights to builders in growth zones
Developers transfer completed buildings between different sites
